policy: A row is VERIFIED only when this session retrieved the cited document itself (page-fetched / pdf-fetched / github-api / repo-snapshot with a committed hash). A row found only in a search-result snippet of an official domain is PARTIAL. Nothing is promoted to VERIFIED by repetition, by a secondary site, or by agreement with another source. Values that could not be read from an official document are left blank and flagged.

sources.title: Official NFL Injury Report - Week 10 of the 2026 season (league view)
sources.establishes: Per-club practice participation status and game status for Week 10, 2026, including the San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys blocks for the 4:25 PM ET Sunday game, and club win-loss records shown in the matchup headers.
sources.notes: Retrieved in chunks; the 49ers/Cowboys block was read directly from the fetched page. The page renders with client-side JavaScript; the retrieval proxy reported an unsupported-browser notice, so rows outside the fetched chunks are not covered by this session (see IR-034).

sources.title: Official Latest NFL Injury Report for Players - Week 10 of the 2026 Season
sources.establishes: That the live injury report is organised by game (date, kickoff ET, TV), with columns Player / Position / Injuries / Practice Status / Game Status, and that week and season are selectable (WEEK 1..WEEK 10, 1965..2026).
sources.notes: Confirms the exact schema the collector must parse, and that a blank Game Status cell is a normal state, not a missing value (see nfl-injury-policy).

sources.title: Competition Committee approves revisions to injury report
sources.establishes: Official definitions: Practice Report = Did Not Participate / Limited Participation (<100% of normal reps) / Full Participation (100%); Game Status = Out (will not play) / Doubtful (unlikely) / Questionable (uncertain); 'Probable' was eliminated because ~95% of Probable players played; a player certain to play is NOT listed in the Game Status Report; deactivating an unlisted player requires an explanation to the league and carries possible discipline.
sources.notes: This is why blank Game Status cells on the Week 10 page are informative rather than missing data. Undated in the retrieved text; the rule set is the one still reflected in the published report columns (see IR-029 for the currency caveat).

sources.title: NFL training camp roster FAQs: Defining injured reserve, PUP list, NFI and more
sources.establishes: Reserve/Injured: no limit on the number of players placed, but a cap of eight designated-to-return per club, a player may be designated twice, and a player must remain on the list at least four games; Reserve/PUP and NFI starters must miss the first four games (down from six before 2022); practice squads up to 16 players from 2022 (12 in 2020-21); Reserve/Suspended players do not count toward roster limits; the article cites Calvin Ridley's suspension through the 2022 season for betting.
sources.notes: Article is written around the 2022 offseason (its dates and examples are 2022); treat the rule text as last-known-official and re-confirm against the current year's roster rules before relying on it (open question Q-09, flag IR-029).

sources.title: Players now eligible to return from injured reserve after four games; practice squads increased to 16 players
sources.establishes: The 2022 amendment set: four-game minimum before return, eight return designations per club, two per player, 16-man practice squads, three elevations per player per season (up from two).
sources.notes: Text read from the search-result rendering of the official nfl.com page; the page itself was not retrieved in this session. Not used as the sole basis for any value row - the same facts are carried by nfl-roster-faq, which was fetched.

sources.title: San Francisco 49ers Depth Chart (updated as of 11/10/26)
sources.establishes: Official club depth chart by position group with first/second/third strings where listed, and the club's own 'Updated as of' date. Several positions list only one or two players.
sources.notes: The club publishes one depth chart page; the same URL pattern (club-site /team/depth-chart) is the collection target for the other 31 clubs. No league-wide depth chart endpoint was found on nfl.com in this session (the nfl.com team depth-chart path returned a 404 page), so per-club sites are the only official source (Q-10, IR-036).

sources.title: NFL Pro FAQ's and Answers (Next Gen Stats, availability and latency)
sources.establishes: Next Gen Stats is the NFL-operated player-tracking system capturing location, speed and acceleration for every player on every play; NGS data is available the day after the game, while Box Score and Play By Play update live during the game; NFL Pro 'matchup advantage' is a composite of success rate, EPA per play and total EPA; NFL Fantasy scoring referenced is full PPR; preseason film and data are not available through NFL Pro.
sources.notes: Sets the hard data-latency constraint for any snap/participation-driven signal: same-day modelling must use play-by-play, not NGS.

sources.title: Colorado Division of Gaming - Sports Betting Taxes Show Continued Growth, $4.7 million collected In September (Nov 5, 2026)
sources.org: Colorado Department of Revenue, Division of Gaming
sources.establishes: September 2026 statewide handle $546,819,852.87 (+40.88% vs August 2026, -10.18% vs September 2025 $608,767,705.13); tax $4,743,419.32 (+50.35% month over month, +46.58% year over year); August 2026 handle $388,148,758.21 and tax $3,154,842.89; fiscal-year-to-date wagers $1,421,300,215.65 and taxes $12,461,150.92. Also publishes the responsible-gambling instruction (BetSmart.Colorado.gov; call or text 1-800-GAMBLER).
sources.notes: State tax figures, not operator gross gaming revenue; do not read a hold percentage off these numbers without the operator-level proceeds report (see co-monthly-index).

sources.title: Colorado Sports Betting Monthly Proceeds Reports (index)
sources.org: Colorado Department of Revenue, Division of Gaming
sources.establishes: The official monthly operator-level proceeds reports exist as PDFs back to 2023 and earlier, including revised versions (e.g. 'September 2026 Sports Betting Proceeds Report', 'April 2026 ... (revised November 2026)'), plus a 'Three Years of Sports Betting In Colorado By the Numbers - Top 10 Sports by Total Wagers' file.

sources.title: New Jersey DGE - DGE Announces August 2026 Gaming Revenue Results (released September 16, 2026)
sources.org: New Jersey Office of the Attorney General, Division of Gaming Enforcement
sources.establishes: August 2026 Sports Wagering Revenue $61,445,421 (-25.0% vs $81,901,788 in August 2025), split Online Sportsbook $59,749,699 and Sportsbook Lounge $1,695,722; year-to-date through August 2026 $671,371,105 (-5.3% vs $708,682,102); total sports wagering taxes $12,767,931 for the month and $140,067,622 year-to-date; tax rates 19.75% online gross revenue and 8.5% lounge plus 1.25% additional.

sources.title: The Odds API - NFL Odds API (endpoint, markets, bookmakers, history)
sources.establishes: A concrete, self-described feed for NFL market prices: sport key americanfootball_nfl; regions us, us2, uk, eu, au; markets h2h (moneyline), spreads, totals, quarter/half and NFL player props (props only from US and AU booksmakers); per-event payload carries commence_time, home_team, away_team and per-bookmaker last_update with price and point; historical odds available from mid-2020 for the featured markets; a free API key tier exists.
sources.notes: Vendor documentation is official only for the vendor's own product. It establishes availability and field names, not data quality, coverage or licence terms; a trial is still required (Q-01, SG-01).

sources.title: Szalkowski & Nelson (2012), 'The Performance of Betting Lines for Predicting the Outcome of NFL Games', arXiv:1211.4000
sources.establishes: From the abstract: 2,560 games (all post-expansion regular- and post-season games 2002-2011); home teams beat the spread 47% of the time; a 2002-2011 strategy of betting home underdogs would have produced 53.5% cumulative against a stated 52.38% break-even threshold; the line difference could retroactively predict divisional winners with no less than 75% accuracy.
sources.notes: Peer-review status not established; the paper is a decade-old sample, so it is a methodology reference and a prior, not evidence that any edge still exists. The 'only ~10% of games move 2+ points' and 'opening vs closing line not significantly different' statements come from the full-text PDF as rendered in search results and are PARTIAL (see IR-030).

sources.title: DraftKings Sportsbook house rules at Golden Nugget Lake Charles (retail house rules v15)
sources.org: DraftKings (operator rules published by a licensed retail casino)
sources.establishes: Operator treatment of correlated and multi-leg wagers: outside a Same Game Parlay or Progressive Parlay, 'any Parlay bet that includes two or more Selections where the outcomes of the Selections are correlated' may be void; a non-SGP parlay 'shall never include two or more offers where the outcomes of which might turn out to be related'; void legs inside a pre-live SGP cause a reprice, and all-void/push causes a void; a wager accepted after the event started is No Action.
sources.notes: Read from the search-result rendering of the operator's own published house-rule PDF; the PDF was not retrieved in this session (proxy failure, IR-030). Rules differ by operator and state; every one of these is a hard constraint on parlay construction and must be re-read from the operator that will actually settle the bet (Q-06, Q-07).

sources.title: Indiana Gaming Commission 68 IAC 27 (sports wagering) - wager and source-of-data requirements
sources.establishes: A regulator's rule that an operator may only accept a sports wager for an event where the outcome can be verified, can be generated by a reliable and independent process, is not affected by any wager placed, and the event is conducted in conformity with applicable law; the commission reserves the right to disapprove a data source.
sources.notes: Used only to show that settlement/data sources are regulated, which constrains any 'originate our own line and settle against it' plan. The current codified text (68 IAC 27-7-4) should be read from iar.iga.in.gov before relying on it (Q-13). The document retrieved by search is the 2020 emergency rule, not the final codified rule.

sources.title: GitHub API: repository 'NFL/Next-Gen-Stats'
sources.establishes: HTTP 404 'Not Found' for the repository that circulating tutorials claim holds downloadable official Next Gen Stats CSVs; a GitHub repository search for the same name returned only third-party scrapers (for example 'Deryck97/nfl_nextgenstats_data', described as 'Weekly data scraped from NFL Next Gen Stats website').
sources.notes: Verified from the sandbox using the GitHub REST API on 2026-11-13. Establishes that no official NFL bulk-tracking download was found; it does not prove none exists elsewhere. Flagged as IR-027.
